title: First pullback after a strong bull spike
body:
> The market became Always In Long through consecutive strong bull bars closing near their highs. The breakout had follow-through, demonstrating urgency and limited selling pressure. The first pullback is shallow, and the bear bars are small and overlapping. I will buy above the first credible bull reversal bar. My thesis is wrong if bears break strongly below the spike base or important higher low. I will target a test of the high and then a measured move. I require at least 1R–1.5R to the first realistic target.

Why it works:

* Bulls who missed the spike want the first pullback.
* Bears have not demonstrated control.
* Early shorts may cover above the signal bar.
* The first pullback in a strong trend often remains brief.

Avoid when:

* The spike terminates directly at major resistance.
* The spike is climactic after an already mature trend.
* The pullback contains strong consecutive bear bars.
location: First shallow pullback after a bull breakout
evidence: Large bull bodies and weak, overlapping bear responses
trigger: A completed bull signal followed by a break above its high
invalidation: A strong break below the protected higher low or spike base
target: Prior spike high; reassess before a measured move
avoid: The spike runs straight into major resistance or the pullback becomes a bear breakout

title: First rally after a strong bear spike
body:
> The market became Always In Short through strong bear bars with closes near their lows and good follow-through. The first rally consists of small, overlapping bull bars and cannot reclaim the breakout point. I will sell below a bear signal bar or after the weak rally turns down. My thesis is wrong above the spike high or last meaningful lower high. I will target the low and a possible measured move.

Participant logic:

* Bears who missed the breakdown sell the first rally.
* Bulls who bought the initial low exit when the rally fails.
* The weak pullback shows limited buying pressure.
location: First weak rally after a bear breakout
evidence: Bear follow-through persists; bulls cannot reclaim the breakdown
trigger: A completed bear signal followed by a break below its low
invalidation: Acceptance above the protected lower high
target: Prior spike low; then the next downside magnet
avoid: Consecutive strong bull bars replace the weak rally

title: H2 pullback in a bull trend
body:
> The market is Always In Long with higher highs, higher lows and repeated buying near the EMA. The first attempt to resume the trend failed, but the pullback remained weak and above structural support. Bears now make a second attempt to push down and fail. I will buy the H2 trigger above a bull signal bar. My thesis is wrong below the pullback low. I will target the prior high and evaluate a runner toward the channel projection.

Important distinction:

An H2 is not automatically bullish. It is strongest when:

* The market is already AIL.
* The pullback is weak.
* The signal occurs at support.
* There is sufficient room to the target.
location: Structural support during a bull pullback
evidence: The first resumption attempt fails, but sellers cannot establish control
trigger: The second upward attempt clears its signal bar
invalidation: A break below the pullback structure
avoid: An H2 forms directly beneath range resistance with little reward available

title: L2 rally in a bear trend
body: > The market is Always In Short, and rallies repeatedly fail near the EMA or prior support-turned-resistance. The first attempt to resume the bear trend failed, but bulls could not create a strong reversal. The second rally stalls with a bear signal bar. I will sell the L2 trigger. My thesis is wrong above the rally high. I will target the prior low and a possible new measured-move low.
location: Resistance during a bear-trend rally
evidence: The first downward attempt fails without creating a bull reversal
trigger: The second downward attempt breaks its signal bar
invalidation: A break above the rally structure
avoid: An L2 sits on major support or the rally shows sustained bull pressure

title: Weak pullback to the EMA in a strong bull trend
body:
> Bulls remain in control because pullbacks are brief, bear bars lack follow-through, and closes remain predominantly above the EMA. Price has returned to the EMA without strong selling pressure. I will buy only after buyers respond with a bull signal bar or failed bear breakout. My thesis is wrong below the structural higher low, not merely a few ticks below the EMA. I will target the prior high.

The EMA is only a location. The actual reason is:

* Strong bull context
* Weak bear response
* Renewed buying at the location
location: EMA near a protected higher low
evidence: The decline is weak; buying resumes at the location
trigger: Bull response or failed bear breakout at the EMA
invalidation: Failure of the higher low, not an arbitrary distance below the average
avoid: The EMA is falling in a balanced range or sellers have strong follow-through

title: Weak rally to the EMA in a strong bear trend
body: > Bears remain in control because rallies are brief, bull bars lack follow-through, and sellers repeatedly defend the EMA. Price has rallied to the EMA but cannot establish acceptance above it. I will sell below a bear reversal bar. My thesis is wrong above the structural lower high. I will target the prior low.
location: EMA near a protected lower high
evidence: The rally is weak; selling resumes at the location
trigger: Bear response or failed bull breakout at the EMA
invalidation: Failure of the lower high, not an arbitrary distance above the average
avoid: The average is rising and bulls are breaking above structure

title: Breakout pullback in a bull trend
body:
> Bulls broke above meaningful resistance with a strong close and follow-through. The pullback returned to the breakout point, but sellers could not push decisively back into the old range. Traders who sold the prior resistance are trapped, and bulls who missed the breakout may buy the retest. I will buy after the breakout point holds and a bull trigger forms. My thesis is wrong if price is accepted back inside the old range. I will target the breakout high and measured move.

Evidence of acceptance back inside the range:

* Multiple closes inside
* Strong bear bars
* Failed attempts to resume upward
* Breakout point acting as resistance again
location: Retest of former resistance
evidence: The breakout has follow-through and the retest holds outside the old range
trigger: Bull signal after the breakout point holds
invalidation: Sustained acceptance back inside the prior range
avoid: The retest penetrates deeply into the range with strong bear closes

title: Bear breakout pullback
body: > Bears broke below support with strong follow-through. Price rallied to retest the breakout point but could not regain the old range. Bulls who bought the old support are trapped, and bears who missed the breakout are selling the retest. I will sell after the pullback forms a bear trigger. My thesis is wrong if price establishes acceptance back above the breakout point. I will target the low and measured move.
location: Retest of former support
evidence: The breakdown holds and old buyers cannot reclaim support
trigger: Bear signal after the retest fails
invalidation: Sustained acceptance back above the breakdown level
avoid: Strong bull closes regain the old range

title: Spike-and-channel bull continuation
body:
> A strong bull spike established Always In Long. The market transitioned into an orderly bull channel with pullbacks that remain weak and attract buyers. I will buy near the lower channel boundary, EMA or prior breakout point after a failed bear attempt. My thesis is wrong below the last structural higher low or after a decisive bear breakout with follow-through. I will target the channel high and scale out near measured-move magnets.

Caution:

As the channel matures, the probability of a deeper correction increases. Late-channel buying requires better location and smaller expectations.
location: Lower edge of an orderly bull channel
evidence: Pullbacks remain corrective after the initial spike
trigger: Failed bear attempt at a channel support area
invalidation: Bear breakout through the last higher low with follow-through
avoid: The channel is mature, crowded into resistance, or already breaking down

title: Spike-and-channel bear continuation
body: > A strong bear spike established Always In Short. The market is descending in a bear channel, and rallies show limited buying pressure. I will sell near the upper channel boundary, EMA or prior breakdown point after a failed bull attempt. My thesis is wrong above the last structural lower high. I will target the channel low and measured-move magnets.
location: Upper edge of an orderly bear channel
evidence: Rallies remain corrective after the initial spike
trigger: Failed bull attempt at channel resistance
invalidation: Bull breakout above the last lower high with follow-through
avoid: The channel is exhausting into major support

title: Small-pullback bull trend
body:
> The market is in a small-pullback bull trend. Pullbacks last only one to three bars, bears cannot reach the EMA consistently, and attempts to short fail quickly. Waiting for a deep discount may leave me without an entry. I will buy a brief pause, H1 or small breakout after a strong close, using reduced size and a structural stop. My thesis is wrong if the market forms a meaningful lower high and strong bear breakout. I will use realistic trend-continuation targets rather than waiting for a large pullback.

This is one of the circumstances where a later, higher-price entry may have greater probability than an early countertrend attempt.
location: Brief pause in a small-pullback bull trend
evidence: Bears cannot sustain even a modest correction
trigger: Renewed bull pressure after a pause or H1
invalidation: A meaningful lower high followed by a strong bear break
avoid: A wide entry bar makes the structural stop unaffordable

title: Small-pullback bear trend
body: > The market is in a small-pullback bear trend. Bulls cannot sustain rallies or reach meaningful resistance. I will sell a brief pause or L1 after renewed bear pressure. My thesis is wrong above the last structural lower high. I will target continuation to the next measured-move or support magnet.
location: Brief pause in a small-pullback bear trend
evidence: Bulls repeatedly fail to sustain a rally
trigger: Renewed bear pressure after a pause or L1
invalidation: A meaningful higher low followed by a strong bull break
avoid: A selloff is already at support with insufficient remaining reward

title: Trend resumption after a two-legged correction
body:
> The market remains Always In Long, but it has entered a two-legged correction. Both legs down failed to produce a strong bear breakout, and the second leg reached support with declining selling pressure. I will buy after the second leg forms a credible reversal or failed breakout. My thesis is wrong below the correction low. I will target the prior high.

Mirror-short:

> The market remains Always In Short. A two-legged rally reached resistance, but bulls failed to create a strong breakout. I will sell after the second leg turns down, with invalidation above the correction high and a target at the prior low.
location: Second corrective leg into trend support
evidence: Both countertrend legs fail to produce a change of control
trigger: Reversal after the second leg and renewed trend pressure
invalidation: Failure of the correction extreme
avoid: The second leg is accelerating rather than losing pressure

title: Trend resumption after a deep pullback
body:
> The market was strongly bullish, but the pullback is deep enough to create uncertainty. I will not assume the bull trend remains intact merely because price is lower. I require a failed bear breakout, a higher low, strong bull reversal and follow-through before buying. My thesis is wrong below the new reversal structure. I will initially target the prior lower high or range midpoint rather than automatically expecting a new high.

A deep pullback often means the market may be transitioning into a range. Expectations should be smaller.
location: New reversal structure after a deep pullback
evidence: The old trend is uncertain; buyers must rebuild evidence
trigger: Failed breakdown, higher low, and bull follow-through
invalidation: Failure of the newly formed reversal low
target: Prior lower high or range midpoint
avoid: The only argument is that price is cheaper than the old high

title: Final-flag breakout continuation
body:
> The market is trending strongly and has paused in a small flag near the extreme. The breakout resumes with strength and follow-through. I will enter only if there is enough room to the next magnet and the breakout has not already become climactic. My thesis is wrong if the breakout immediately fails back into the flag. I will target the measured move while recognizing that the final flag may precede exhaustion.

“Final flag” is usually identifiable only in hindsight. Treat it as a warning about diminishing reward, not a command to reverse immediately.
location: Late flag close to a trend extreme
evidence: Continuation is still strong, but the trend is mature
trigger: Flag breakout with follow-through and room to a target
invalidation: Immediate failed breakout back into the flag
avoid: The breakout is climactic or its target is too close

title: Failed bear breakout below a range
body:
> The market is in a trading range. Price broke below the range low, but bears failed to obtain follow-through and price closed back inside. Breakout sellers are trapped, and range traders are buying low. I will buy above the bull reversal bar. My thesis is wrong below the failed-breakout low. I will target the range midpoint first and the upper range only if buying pressure develops.

Best evidence:

* Breakout bar has a prominent tail.
* Next bar closes back inside.
* Repeated selling below the low fails.
* Bull reversal has follow-through.
location: Just below a mature range low
evidence: Sellers break support but cannot sustain prices below it
trigger: Reclaim into the range followed by a bull trigger
invalidation: Failure below the rejected breakout low
avoid: Price is accepting below the range in a strong bear breakout

title: Failed bull breakout above a range
body: > The market is in a trading range. Price broke above the range high, but bulls failed to obtain follow-through and price returned inside. Breakout buyers are trapped, and range traders are selling high. I will sell below a bear reversal bar. My thesis is wrong above the failed-breakout high. I will target the midpoint first and the lower range if selling pressure strengthens.
location: Just above a mature range high
evidence: Buyers break resistance but cannot sustain prices above it
trigger: Return into the range followed by a bear trigger
invalidation: Failure above the rejected breakout high
avoid: Price is accepting above the range in a strong bull breakout

title: Second-entry buy near the bottom of a range
body:
> Price is in the lower third of a mature range. The first bull reversal attempt failed, but bears could not obtain continuation below the low. A second bull attempt is forming with better buying pressure. I will buy the second-entry trigger. My thesis is wrong below the range extreme. I will target the midpoint.

The second entry matters because the bears failed twice to create continuation.
location: Lower edge of a mature trading range
evidence: Sellers fail twice to achieve downside continuation
trigger: Second bull trigger at the range edge
invalidation: Break below the range extreme
avoid: The second attempt develops in the middle of the range

title: Second-entry sell near the top of a range
body: > Price is in the upper third of a mature range. The first reversal down failed, but bulls could not sustain the breakout. A second bear attempt forms after buying pressure weakens. I will sell below the second-entry signal. My thesis is wrong above the range extreme. I will target the midpoint.
location: Upper edge of a mature trading range
evidence: Buyers fail twice to achieve upside continuation
trigger: Second bear trigger at the range edge
invalidation: Break above the range extreme
avoid: The second attempt is a pause in a strong bull breakout

title: Double-bottom bull flag inside a range
body:
> The broader market is a trading range, but the current swing has bullish pressure. Price tests a prior low and fails to break meaningfully below it. The second low forms with less selling pressure and a credible bull trigger. I will buy above the signal bar. My thesis is wrong below the double bottom. I will target the range midpoint or prior swing high.

A double bottom is better when the second low demonstrates failure, not merely equal price.
location: Retest of a range swing low
evidence: The second test cannot establish new selling pressure
trigger: Bull signal above the second-bottom structure
invalidation: Failure below the double bottom
avoid: Equal lows appear without rejection or a credible trigger

title: Double-top bear flag inside a range
body: > Price retests a prior high but cannot establish acceptance above it. The second high shows weaker buying pressure or a failed breakout. I will sell below a bear signal bar. My thesis is wrong above the double top. I will target the midpoint or prior swing low.
location: Retest of a range swing high
evidence: The second test cannot establish new buying pressure
trigger: Bear signal below the second-top structure
invalidation: Failure above the double top
avoid: Equal highs appear without rejection or a credible trigger

title: Range-edge reversal after a vacuum test
body:
> Price accelerated toward the range low because traders expected the magnet to be tested, and countertrend buyers temporarily stepped aside. The fast move may be a vacuum rather than new sustained selling pressure. I will not buy merely because the magnet was reached. I require the breakout to fail, price to return inside the range and buyers to create a credible reversal. My thesis is wrong below the vacuum extreme. I will target the midpoint.

Key principle:

A vacuum move can look strong even when it is primarily caused by the absence of opposition. Wait for the market’s response at the magnet.
location: Accelerating test of a range low
evidence: The fast move reaches a magnet, then sellers fail
trigger: Failed breakdown and confirmed return into the range
invalidation: Failure below the vacuum extreme
avoid: Buying simply because the move was fast or touched support

title: Vacuum rally into range resistance
body: > Price accelerated toward the range high as sellers stepped aside and traders anticipated a test of resistance. The rally may reflect a vacuum rather than durable buying pressure. I will not sell simply because price reached resistance. I require a failed breakout, bearish response and return into the range. My thesis is wrong above the vacuum extreme. I will target the midpoint.
location: Accelerating test of a range high
evidence: The rally reaches a magnet, then buyers fail
trigger: Failed breakout and confirmed return into the range
invalidation: Failure above the vacuum extreme
avoid: Selling the first touch without rejection

title: Range scalp after disappointment
body:
> Bulls attempted to break above the middle or upper portion of the range, but the breakout was weak and immediately disappointed buyers. Because the market remains balanced, I will sell after the failed attempt, using a modest target near the midpoint. My thesis is wrong if bulls create a strong breakout with follow-through.

Disappointment creates exits:

* Bulls exit weak longs.
* Countertrend bears enter.
* Profit-taking accelerates the move back toward equilibrium.
location: Middle-to-upper part of a balanced range
evidence: A weak bull breakout disappoints its buyers
trigger: Bear response after the failed bull attempt
invalidation: Strong bull breakout with follow-through
avoid: The proposed scalp has poor reward after costs

title: Breakout-mode range
body:
> The market is compressed with repeated reversals, tight overlapping bars and failed attempts in both directions. Neither side has demonstrated control. I will not predict the breakout. I will wait for a strong breakout with follow-through or a breakout pullback. My thesis after entry will be wrong if price immediately returns into the tight range. The target will be a measured move based on the range height.

In breakout mode:

* Direction is close to neutral.
* Stop-entry traders may be trapped repeatedly.
* Position size should reflect the risk of a false breakout.
* The middle of the range offers poor trader’s equations.
location: Tight overlap with no accepted direction
evidence: Breakouts in both directions repeatedly fail
trigger: Wait for a directional breakout and follow-through, then reassess
invalidation: A later breakout thesis fails if price returns into compression
target: Range-height projection only after a valid breakout
avoid: Predicting direction from the middle of the compression

title: Failed breakout followed by an opposite breakout
body:
> Bulls broke above the range but failed, trapping breakout buyers. Price then crossed the range and broke below support with strong follow-through. The failed bull breakout increased the probability that the successful move could be down. I will sell the bear breakout pullback. My thesis is wrong if price regains the range. I will target a measured move below the range.

The mirror applies after a failed bear breakout followed by a strong bull breakout.
location: Opposite boundary after a failed breakout
evidence: One side is trapped and the other achieves real follow-through
trigger: Pullback after the opposite-side breakout
invalidation: Regaining and accepting inside the old range
target: Measured move beyond the new breakout
avoid: The opposite breakout also lacks follow-through

title: Broadening range reversal
body: > Price has formed higher highs and lower lows, showing expanding volatility but poor directional control. A new extreme alone is not a breakout. I will fade an extreme only after rejection and a credible reversal trigger. My thesis is wrong beyond that extreme. I will target the middle rather than automatically expecting the opposite boundary.
location: Rejected extreme of an expanding range
evidence: Higher highs and lower lows reveal poor directional control
trigger: Rejection and reversal at an outer extreme
invalidation: A break beyond the rejected extreme
avoid: Mistaking every new extreme for trend confirmation

title: Middle-of-range avoidance
body:
> The market is in a trading range, and price is currently near the midpoint. Both the upside and downside targets are too close relative to a structural stop. I have no favorable trader’s equation. I will remain flat until price reaches an edge or breaks out with follow-through.

This is a valid thesis: **no trade**.
location: Middle of a trading range
evidence: Nearby targets are small relative to a structural stop
trigger: No entry; wait for an edge or accepted breakout
invalidation: Reassess only when location or market state changes
avoid: Inventing an entry because standing aside feels unproductive

title: Major trend reversal from bull to bear
body:
> The market has been Always In Long, but the trend is mature and buying pressure is weakening. Bears broke the bull trend line with strength. Bulls then retested the high but failed to resume the trend, creating a lower high or failed breakout. I will sell below a bear signal bar after the failed test. My thesis is wrong above the retest high. I will target the prior higher low, EMA and possible measured move.

The trend-line break alone is insufficient. The failed test supplies stronger evidence that control may be changing.
location: Failed high retest after a bull trend-line break
evidence: Bulls cannot resume the trend after a meaningful bear response
trigger: Bear trigger after the lower high or failed new high
invalidation: Break above the retest high
target: Prior higher low or nearest support
avoid: Selling a trend-line break before testing bull strength

title: Major trend reversal from bear to bull
body: > The market has been Always In Short, but selling pressure is weakening. Bulls broke the bear trend line with strength. Bears retested the low but failed to resume the trend, forming a higher low or failed breakdown. I will buy above a bull signal bar after the failed test. My thesis is wrong below the retest low. I will target the prior lower high, EMA and possible measured move.
location: Failed low retest after a bear trend-line break
evidence: Bears cannot resume the trend after a meaningful bull response
trigger: Bull trigger after the higher low or failed new low
invalidation: Break below the retest low
target: Prior lower high or nearest resistance
avoid: Buying a trend-line break without a failed resumption test

title: Wedge bottom
body:
> The bear trend has made three pushes down, with each push producing less sustained selling or increasing overlap. The third push reaches support and fails to continue. I will buy only after a bull reversal signal or strong break above the bear micro-channel. My thesis is wrong below the wedge low. I will target the EMA, prior lower high or beginning of the final leg down.

The wedge creates potential because:

* Late bears may be exhausted.
* Early bears take profits.
* Countertrend bulls enter.
* A failed third push traps sellers.

Three pushes alone are insufficient if every push remains powerful.
location: Third push down reaching support
evidence: New lows have weakening follow-through or greater overlap
trigger: Bull reversal or break of the bear micro-channel
invalidation: Break below the wedge extreme
target: Prior lower high or origin of the final leg
avoid: All three pushes remain powerful and closes remain bearish

title: Wedge top
body: > The bull trend has produced three pushes higher, but follow-through is deteriorating and the third push reaches resistance or overshoots the channel. I will sell only after a bear reversal signal or clear break below the bull micro-channel. My thesis is wrong above the wedge high. I will target the EMA, prior higher low or beginning of the final leg up.
location: Third push up reaching resistance
evidence: New highs have weakening follow-through or greater overlap
trigger: Bear reversal or break of the bull micro-channel
invalidation: Break above the wedge extreme
target: Prior higher low or origin of the final leg
avoid: All three pushes remain powerful and closes remain bullish

title: Parabolic wedge bottom
body:
> The bear trend is accelerating through multiple increasingly steep pushes. The move is climactic, but strong momentum means buying early is dangerous. I will wait for a strong bull reversal, failed attempt to resume down and follow-through before buying. My thesis is wrong below the climax low. I will target at least a two-legged correction toward the EMA.

A climax increases reversal probability but does not tell you precisely when the reversal begins.
location: Accelerating selloff into a climax
evidence: Momentum is extreme; exhaustion still needs confirmation
trigger: Bull reversal, failed bear resumption, and follow-through
invalidation: Break below the climax low
target: First resistance in a potential two-legged correction
avoid: Buying an accelerating decline before sellers fail

title: Parabolic wedge top
body: > The bull trend is accelerating through increasingly steep pushes. The move is climactic and vulnerable to profit-taking, but I will not sell solely because price appears too high. I require a bear reversal, failed bull resumption and follow-through. My thesis is wrong above the climax high. I will target a two-legged correction toward the EMA.
location: Accelerating rally into a climax
evidence: Momentum is extreme; exhaustion still needs confirmation
trigger: Bear reversal, failed bull resumption, and follow-through
invalidation: Break above the climax high
target: First support in a potential two-legged correction
avoid: Selling an accelerating rally before buyers fail

title: Buy climax followed by failed continuation
body:
> Bulls created unusually large bars, expanded range and urgent buying late in an existing bull move. After the climax, bulls attempted another breakout but could not obtain follow-through. I will sell only after bears demonstrate control through a credible reversal and failed bull retest. My thesis is wrong above the climax high. I will target the EMA or base of the climax.

Do not automatically short a buy climax. Strong trends can produce repeated climaxes.
location: Late bull climax followed by a weak new high
evidence: Urgent buying is followed by failed continuation
trigger: Bear control after a failed bull retest
invalidation: Break above the climax extreme
target: EMA area or base of the climax
avoid: Assuming every large bull bar ends the trend

title: Sell climax followed by failed continuation
body: > Bears created unusually large bars and urgent selling late in an existing decline. Bears then attempted continuation but failed, and price reclaimed the climax area. I will buy after a credible bull reversal and failed bear retest. My thesis is wrong below the climax low. I will target the EMA or origin of the final selloff.
location: Late bear climax followed by a weak new low
evidence: Urgent selling is followed by failed continuation
trigger: Bull control after a failed bear retest
invalidation: Break below the climax extreme
target: EMA area or origin of the final selloff
avoid: Assuming every large bear bar ends the trend

title: Micro double bottom after a climax
body: > The market experienced a sell climax and bounced. Bears retested the low but failed to break it decisively, creating a micro double bottom. I will buy above the bull trigger only if the retest shows reduced selling pressure. My thesis is wrong below the second low. I will target the EMA or next resistance.
location: Close retest of a sell-climax low
evidence: The second low attracts less selling and is rejected
trigger: Bull trigger after the small double bottom
invalidation: Failure of the second-low structure
avoid: Treating a visual double bottom as confirmation by itself

title: Micro double top after a climax
body: > The market experienced a buy climax and pulled back. Bulls retested the high but failed to resume the trend, creating a micro double top. I will sell below the bear trigger if buying pressure has weakened. My thesis is wrong above the second high. I will target the EMA or next support.
location: Close retest of a buy-climax high
evidence: The second high attracts less buying and is rejected
trigger: Bear trigger after the small double top
invalidation: Failure of the second-high structure
avoid: Treating a visual double top as confirmation by itself

title: Failed final flag
body:
> A mature bull trend formed a final flag and broke higher, but the breakout immediately failed and returned below the flag. Breakout buyers are trapped, and earlier bulls may take profits. I will sell after bearish confirmation. My thesis is wrong above the failed-breakout high. I will target the opposite side of the flag and then the EMA.

Mirror:

> A mature bear trend broke below a final flag but immediately reversed above it. Breakout sellers are trapped. I will buy after bullish confirmation, with invalidation below the failed breakout and targets at the flag high and EMA.
location: Failed breakout from a mature trend flag
evidence: Late breakout traders lose their expected continuation
trigger: Opposite-side confirmation back through the flag
invalidation: Renewed acceptance beyond the failed breakout extreme
target: Opposite flag edge, then EMA area
avoid: Calling a flag final before an actual failure

title: Channel overshoot and reversal
body:
> The bull channel has persisted for many bars. Price overshot the upper channel line, but the breakout failed and produced a strong bear response. I will not sell the overshoot alone. I will sell after bearish follow-through or a failed retest of the high. My thesis is wrong above the overshoot high. I will target the EMA or lower channel area.

The mirror applies to a bear-channel undershoot followed by a failed breakout and bullish reversal.
location: Outside a mature channel boundary
evidence: The overshoot fails and the market returns to the channel
trigger: Opposite follow-through or a failed extreme retest
invalidation: Break beyond the overshoot high or low
target: EMA area or opposite channel area
avoid: Trading the overshoot alone

title: MA-gap-bar reversal
body:
> The market has remained far from the EMA during a strong trend. Price finally pulls back and produces the first bar whose high or low no longer overlaps the EMA area in the usual way, signaling a possible change in pressure. I will not reverse solely because of the MA-gap condition. I require a trend-line break, test and failed resumption. My thesis is wrong beyond the tested extreme. I will target a deeper correction or opposite-side structure.

The MA-gap bar is supporting evidence, not a standalone entry.
location: A bar fully separated from the moving average
evidence: Separation is context; it does not prove a trend reversal
trigger: For a reversal thesis, require a trend break and failed resumption test
invalidation: Failure of the tested reversal extreme
target: Nearest opposing structure before a deeper correction
avoid: Confusing a gap bar with an automatic reversal signal

title: Trapped bears after a failed breakdown
body: > Bears sold below a visible low, expecting acceleration. The breakout failed, and price returned above the level with a strong bull close. Those bears are trapped and may buy back shorts above the signal bar. I will buy the reversal, with invalidation below the failed-breakout low and a target at the next magnet.
location: Reclaimed support after a breakdown fails
evidence: Breakdown sellers lose acceptance below their entry area
trigger: Strong reclaim followed by a bull entry trigger
invalidation: Failure below the rejected breakdown
avoid: Assuming a wick alone proves sellers are trapped

title: Trapped bulls after a failed breakout
body: > Bulls bought above a visible high, expecting continuation. Price immediately reversed into the prior structure. Breakout buyers are trapped and may sell as price falls below the signal bar. I will sell after confirmation, with invalidation above the failed-breakout high and a target at the next support or range midpoint.
location: Lost resistance after an upside breakout fails
evidence: Breakout buyers lose acceptance above their entry area
trigger: Strong return below the level followed by a bear trigger
invalidation: Failure above the rejected breakout
avoid: Assuming a wick alone proves buyers are trapped

title: Bad stop-entry trap
body: > A visually obvious signal encouraged traders to enter with stops beyond a prior bar, but the entry occurred in poor context—for example, buying an H2 directly beneath range resistance. The market triggered the entry and immediately rejected it. I will trade against the trapped side only after the rejection becomes clear. My thesis is wrong if the original breakout regains acceptance. I will target the opposite side of the local structure.
location: Obvious signal in poor location
evidence: An apparent continuation entry immediately meets opposing structure
trigger: Clear rejection of the original stop-entry setup
invalidation: Acceptance in the direction of the original breakout
target: Opposite side of the local structure
avoid: Fading a signal before it actually fails

title: Countertrend trap in a strong trend
body:
> Countertrend traders repeatedly attempt to reverse a strong bull trend, but every bear breakout lacks follow-through. Their stops above the failed reversal can contribute to continuation. I will buy above the failed bear signal, with invalidation below the pullback and a target at the trend high.

Mirror this in a strong bear trend by selling below failed bull reversal attempts.
location: Failed countertrend attempt inside a strong trend
evidence: Countertrend entries cannot attract follow-through
trigger: Trend-direction break beyond the failed countertrend signal
invalidation: Failure of the trend pullback structure
avoid: The countertrend move has already broken structure with strength

title: Accumulating buying pressure inside a range
body:
> The market remains technically in a range, but bull bars are becoming larger, bear pullbacks are shallower, closes cluster near their highs and price repeatedly tests the upper boundary. I will not buy directly beneath resistance. I will wait for a strong breakout and follow-through or a successful breakout pullback. My thesis is wrong if the breakout returns deeply into the range. I will target a measured move.

Buying pressure changes the odds, but resistance still affects reward.
location: Repeated tests of the upper range boundary
evidence: Stronger bull closes and shallower pullbacks accumulate
trigger: Accepted breakout or successful breakout pullback
invalidation: Deep return and acceptance inside the range
avoid: Buying directly into resistance before it breaks

title: Accumulating selling pressure inside a range
body: > Bear bars are becoming stronger, bull rallies are weaker, closes cluster near their lows and price repeatedly tests support. I will avoid buying merely because the market reached the range low. I will wait for either a failed breakdown or a strong bear breakout with follow-through. If the breakdown succeeds, I will sell the pullback and target a measured move.
location: Repeated tests of the lower range boundary
evidence: Stronger bear closes and weaker rallies accumulate
trigger: Accepted breakdown or successful breakdown pullback
invalidation: Return and acceptance above the broken range low
avoid: Buying the range low despite increasing selling pressure

title: Hidden buying pressure during a bear move
body: > Price continues making lower lows, but each new low is rejected, bear closes weaken, bull bars become more frequent and sellers cannot achieve follow-through. This is evidence of buying pressure, not yet proof of a reversal. I will wait for a trend-line break, higher low and bull trigger before buying. My thesis is wrong below the higher-low structure.
location: Lower lows with increasingly weak selling
evidence: Rejected lows and more bull bars suggest emerging buying
trigger: Trend-line break, higher low, and bull trigger
invalidation: Failure below the higher-low structure
target: Nearest lower high before larger reversal targets
avoid: Treating hidden pressure as a completed reversal

title: Hidden selling pressure during a bull move
body: > Price continues making higher highs, but each new high is rejected, bull closes weaken, bear bars increase and bulls cannot achieve follow-through. I will wait for a trend-line break, lower high and bear trigger before selling. My thesis is wrong above the lower-high structure.
location: Higher highs with increasingly weak buying
evidence: Rejected highs and more bear bars suggest emerging selling
trigger: Trend-line break, lower high, and bear trigger
invalidation: Failure above the lower-high structure
target: Nearest higher low before larger reversal targets
avoid: Treating hidden pressure as a completed reversal

title: Opening gap accepted
body: > ES opened above prior resistance and remained above it. Early attempts to fill the gap failed, and bulls produced strong closes with follow-through. The market is accepting the higher price. I will buy the first credible pullback that holds above the breakout area. My thesis is wrong if price returns into and establishes acceptance within the prior range. I will target the opening measured move or next higher-timeframe magnet.
location: Opening gap above prior resistance
evidence: Early gap-fill attempts fail; strong closes hold higher prices
trigger: First credible pullback that holds the breakout area
invalidation: Acceptance back inside the prior range
target: Opening projection or next higher-timeframe magnet
avoid: Assuming a gap is accepted before observing the response

title: Opening gap rejected
body:
> ES opened above resistance, but the first breakout failed and price returned into the prior day’s range. Overnight buyers are trapped, and the gap may become a vacuum toward the prior close. I will sell after bearish confirmation inside the old range. My thesis is wrong above the failed opening high. I will target the prior close or another internal magnet.

Mirror this for a gap down that is rejected and reclaimed.
location: Opening gap that returns to the old range
evidence: The gap fails to attract continued participation
trigger: Confirmation after returning inside the prior range
invalidation: Break beyond the failed opening extreme
target: Prior close or nearest internal magnet
avoid: Expecting every opening gap to fill

title: Opening reversal after a test of the overnight extreme
body:
> The regular session tested the overnight high, but buyers could not obtain acceptance above it. Price formed a failed breakout and returned below the level. I will sell after a bear trigger, with invalidation above the failed breakout and a target at VWAP, the open or the opposite side of the opening range.

The overnight high is a location. The failed acceptance supplies the trade reason.
location: Test of an overnight extreme during the open
evidence: The regular-session test fails to achieve acceptance
trigger: Opposite-side trigger after reclaiming the level
invalidation: Break beyond the rejected overnight test
target: Open, VWAP area, or nearest opening-range magnet
avoid: Trading the overnight level without rejection evidence

title: Opening range breakout with follow-through
body: > The open formed a balanced range. Price then broke out with strong bars, closes near the extreme and follow-through. I will enter on the breakout pullback rather than chase an overextended bar. My thesis is wrong if price returns into the opening range. I will target a measured move based on the range height.
location: Breakout from a balanced opening range
evidence: Strong breakout bars and subsequent closes show acceptance
trigger: Pullback that holds outside the opening range
invalidation: Return and acceptance inside the opening range
avoid: Chasing a large breakout bar with poor structural reward

title: Opening reversal with no confirmed direction
body:
> The open produced large bars in both directions, repeated reversals and poor follow-through. The market is in breakout mode rather than a confirmed trend. I will remain flat until one side achieves a breakout with follow-through or an edge produces a clear failed breakout.

Again, standing aside is a valid Brooks-style decision.
location: Open with large reversals in both directions
evidence: Follow-through is poor and control is unresolved
trigger: Stay flat until acceptance or a clear edge failure develops
invalidation: Reassess when a directional premise becomes supported
avoid: Taking every opening reversal as a new trend

title: Measured-move magnet during a trend
body: > The market broke from a clear structure and has room to a measured-move projection. Trend pressure remains intact, and there is no strong reversal evidence. I will trade continuation toward the magnet but reduce expectations as price approaches it. The measured move is a target, not an automatic reversal level.
location: Trend approaching a measured projection
evidence: Continuation pressure is intact and room remains
trigger: A valid continuation setup before reaching the magnet
invalidation: Failure of that continuation structure
avoid: Treating a projection as an automatic reversal signal

title: Prior high or low as a vacuum magnet
body:
> Price is close to an obvious prior high, and bears may step aside because a test is likely. I will not short prematurely merely because the market appears overextended. I may trade toward the magnet if trend pressure remains strong. I will consider a reversal only after the test produces rejection, failure and confirmation.

Mirror this when price approaches a prior low.
location: Trend approaching an obvious prior extreme
evidence: Opposition may pause while the market tests the level
trigger: Continuation only with room; reversal only after failure
invalidation: Failure of the chosen continuation or reversal structure
avoid: Fading a strong move simply because it approaches a prior extreme

title: Gap-close magnet
body: > Price has entered a vacuum toward the prior close. Countertrend traders may delay entry until the gap is tested. I will trade toward the gap only while pressure and reward remain favorable. At the magnet, I will take profits or reassess; I will not automatically reverse without evidence of rejection.
location: Price moving toward the prior close
evidence: Pressure favors a gap test while countertrend interest waits
trigger: A valid setup in the direction of the gap-close magnet
invalidation: Failure of the supporting swing structure
avoid: Expecting movement through the magnet without reassessment

title: Early probe at a possible failed breakout
body: > Price is testing a major range low and selling pressure is weakening, but reversal confirmation is incomplete. The potential reward is large relative to the structural risk. I may enter one MES as a probe with a fixed stop below the extreme. If the probe fails, I will accept the loss. I will not add because price becomes cheaper. Full confirmation would justify a separate decision, not a rescue operation.
location: Possible failure at major range support
evidence: Selling weakens, but confirmation is incomplete
trigger: Optional research-only probe under a predefined plan
invalidation: The predefined stop beyond the extreme; no additions
avoid: Using a probe to justify averaging into a losing trade

title: Probe before a major reversal
body: > The trend is climactic and has reached major support, but the market remains Always In Short. I may take a one-MES countertrend probe only if the stop is small relative to the potential two-legged correction. I assume the probability is low and require approximately 2R–3R potential. If sellers continue strongly, I exit without adding.
location: Climactic decline at major support
evidence: Always-In remains short; the reversal is still speculative
trigger: Advanced research-only probe with an accepted fixed loss
invalidation: Continuation through the predefined extreme
avoid: Calling overextension confirmation or enlarging a failed probe

title: Confirmed entry after the probe opportunity passes
body:
> The early reversal entry offered excellent reward but low probability. I declined or lost the probe. The market has now broken the trend line, tested the low and formed a higher low with strong confirmation. I will buy at a higher price because probability has improved. My structural risk and target still produce a favorable equation.

Paying a higher price for stronger evidence can be rational.
location: Higher low after a trend-line break and low test
evidence: Bears fail to resume and buyers supply stronger evidence
trigger: Confirmed bull trigger after the higher low
invalidation: Failure of the new higher-low structure
avoid: Chasing confirmation when too little reward remains
